en: You alone were lion-maned Seytek.
Short is the pointed blade,
Scion of a precious lion,
My mirror left by the noble,
My champion desired by the people,
At every sight of you the heart is reassured;
There is no refuge but you.
A challenger has come to dispute with you;
A heroic lion has come to oppose you—
An enemy named Sarybai.
He is the lion who will wrestle you;
God has granted his wish.
Hero, the term you gave Sarybai
Has now expired, he says;
“Hero, my time to wrestle has come,” he says.
The roaring ravager
Has arrived in all his strength.
He has readied his cartridge pouch
And prepared his powder and shot.
His destructive intent is plain;
He has put on armor no bullet can pierce.
He has made ready his ornamented spear;
The six-layered black earth
Seems to smoke from its depths
Beneath the fearsome boar.
Heed the lord’s words:
A warrior has come to wrestle,
An enemy has come to joust,
An enemy has come to fight.
Shouting as he entered the field,
The enemy of old came as your equal.
Before the terrible scourge that has arrived,
Hero, dread has fallen upon my heart.
If the great host now joins battle,
How can its camp remain settled?
Before the torment of that mighty swine,
What will become of the village?
Watching him, I burned with anguish;
I utterly despaired of life.
I looked, understood, and grieved;
Today I have despaired of precious life.
Not Sarybai but a bullet has come,
A rending flood has swept in;
A fierce force, a mighty conflict—
From the infidel’s wrath,
The black earth itself trembles.”
So saying, the diviner
Stood there delivering his news.
The great drum was made of camel hide,
And was three fathoms thick;
Its hide was camel hide,
And when struck once with an axe,
Its booming rolled out upon the road.
Its thunder spread across the earth;
The wrestler struck it when flight threatened.
Yesterday, when the dawn shone clear,
When light broke through the earth,
When the nightingale sang in the forest
And the cuckoo mourned in the mountains,
When the bright dawn broke,
A booming sound was heard.
When the great drum was struck,
Startled to his fly-like soul,
He saddled Kulansur,
And the fated Seytek rose.
The people cried out in tumult,
Raising a clamorous alarm,
Their banners unfurling in splendor:
“The fearsome foe has come to battle!”
All the champions grew excited,
All the lion-maned warriors were stirred;
The army shouted and surged forward.
Wise men surpassing all in judgment
Proclaimed this conflict aloud;
Commanders of ten shouted fiercely,
And the imposing champions,
Broad-chested and wide-breasted,
Declared that their hearts welcomed his coming.
All the champions grew excited,
All the heroes cried out,
All the wrestlers armed themselves.
Sarybai joined the conflict—
Such was his fierce wrath.
When they grappled, no bullet could pierce him;
Their strength was spent and their power gone.
Life fled, wheeling away,
Gnawing at whoever he met,
Sarybay tormented every soul.
Against that swine whose soul is departing,
Let us all fall upon him,
Let us attack together!
Against that infidel who boasts of his strength,
With an uproar that splits the sky,
Let us charge from every side,
Let us shout and level our spears,
Let us make the battle fierce!
Clashing and grappling,
Thrashing one another like autumn wool,
Becoming like hungry lions,
Spilling blood with our bullets,
Reckless of our lives,
Fighting in fury,
Let us unleash boundless havoc.
Let grim calamity become our sport;
With that dog who ravaged the people,
Let us grapple once!
Let us tear at each other without tiring,
And drink our fill of blood.
Whoever faces us,
Let us hew them down with axes,
Thrusting and stabbing with spears,
Let us fulfill every desire,
Let us meet them face-to-face.
Shouting and fighting,
Let us unleash a furious assault.
Let every spear be stained with blood;
If death comes and our days are done,
Let it be at Sarybay’s hands.
Let countless warriors be slain;
Let us behold the worst ordeal.
Sarybay has gone mad with rage;
Let us test ourselves against him.
Shouting from every side,
Let every battle cry unite in one place,
Let us invoke Manas as our war cry,
And level our spears from every side.
Let us not stand idle—let battle begin;
Let us see how great his strength is,
And die while locked in combat.
Fighting with no thought for life,
If the Almighty so wills,
Let us surrender our precious lives.
This Sarybay seems to have gone mad;
Let me try my strength against him!”
The swine’s torment had gone too far;
Claiming everything as his own,
Rallying their fiercest courage for battle,
Let us unleash a mighty conflict.
Not merely one of us, but all of us—
All of us, beyond counting—
Against the hideous swine,
Against the wrath-filled infidel,
Against the finest warrior who meets us,
Against the burning ember of hell,
Against death’s unerring shaft,
Against his hero’s girded waist,
Against this savage himself,
Let us reach him with battle cries,
And pass amid resounding blows.
Let us unleash a battle;
If death comes, let us die,
And behold a wondrous spectacle.
Sarybay is the enemy we face;
Let us exchange battle cries with him
And see what comes.
The people summoned their courage and surged,
And now they waged a savage battle;
Sarybay was the one they grappled with,
And the melee roared around him.
With fierce courage and great valor,
Every warrior fought without holding back;
The uproar split the sky,
A vast tumult of countless war cries.
Most wondrous was their fierce courage,
And the death of Sarybay.
The people cried out, lending courage,
While the warriors stood in this plight.
The born hero Seytek
Spoke softly, yet with firm resolve,
Addressing the gathered multitude,
And beginning his speech to the people:
“Sarybay, son of the monster,
Has enslaved the falcons,
Has enslaved noble heroes.
He drove off all he encountered,
He began a savage conflict,
Subjugating everyone he caught,
And slaughtering them without exception.
His fame has traveled far;
Do not ask what that madman is like—
His outrages are many.
He grappled, proclaiming himself a man;
For many days they fought for victory.
None who attacked could bring him down,
None could wrestle the dog to defeat.
His cunning is formidable, his venom strong;
When I recall it, the swine seems invincible.
For seven days I fought without rest;
Wounded, my strength has left me,
And I can find no peace.
My heart burns with care,
My people, I stand before you wounded.
All the warriors have grown distraught;
The lion-hearted Külchoro
Was defeated by Sarybay.
Every ear strained in alarm,
And the ordeal seemed endless.
Sarybay, whom I opposed,
Shows himself a bristling savage.
His prowess is beyond measure,
His warrior’s strength beyond reckoning,
And such is his merciless wrath.
Sarybay has wrought a fearful marvel;
Do not despise my words—
This was a desperate deed,
And it has reduced my speech to pleading.
He bent my back low;
Against that infidel Sarybay,
I fought, but lacked the power;
I wrestled, but lacked the strength.
After grappling, no might remained in me;
If I die, I shall have no regret.
My youth has shown itself;
This poor soul despaired of life.
I had drunk my fill of liquor,
And had little sense within me.
Now I am burdened with worry;
I had been drunk on liquor.
The child grieved, his joints going slack,
The poor wretch despairing of life.
The infidel son of the monster
Revealed his savage ferocity;
Like one who had heard his fearsome name,
I despaired of my entrusted life.
Against the grunting boar,
Standing on opposing sides,
For nine full days,
We fought with sodden blows.
Through all nine days,
We wounded every fleshy part.
My ribs were shattered flat,
My breast filled with darkening blood.
This bright world is deeply cherished;
While alive, one cannot help loving life.
‘If only each of us survives’—
Such a longing fills these words.
I have not yet reached my destined prime;
The milk of my mother Chürök’s breast
Has not yet left my palate.
My boundless strength has not yet matured;
My time for wrestling has not yet come.
I am truly still an unripe youth,
A child newly turned fifteen.
If you provoke conflict without fighting,
I, an untried child, will fall into endless woe.
Though Külchoro was born a lion,
He could not defeat him in wrestling;
Ah, tender youth—
He could not overcome the immature dog.
The foe he met was Sarybay;
When they crossed the facing slopes,
When they opposed each other and raised conflict,
When they came face-to-face,
Only a spoonful of my blood remained,
My flesh was left a blue, pulpy mass.
My frail soul shrieked,
